construct: Outer hair cells change length in response to membrane-potential changes through the motor protein prestin in their lateral membrane. This electromotility feeds mechanical energy back into the cochlea, amplifying basilar-membrane motion and sharpening auditory sensitivity and frequency selectivity.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Prestin is the voltage-sensitive motor protein of outer hair cells; loss of prestin abolishes somatic electromotility and cochlear amplification while inner hair cells may remain intact.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Inner hair-cell synaptic machinery is crucial for afferent transmission but cannot explain selective loss of outer-hair-cell electromotility with preserved inner hair cells.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Selective outer-hair-cell electromotility failure and raised thresholds uniquely identify prestin.
